newsitem.title: USA: California unveils small business bond program.
newsitem.headline: California unveils small business bond program.

text.p: California state Treasurer Matt Fong launched a program on Tuesday to give small underwriting, bond counsel and financial advisory firms a larger piece of the state's bond business.
Firms that qualify for the so-called Small Business Enterprise Program would be eligible to participate in bond deals by the state and by its bonding authorities, Fong said.

"Small business is the backbone of the California economy and they should have an opportunity to compete with the bigger firms for the opportunity to do business with and for the state," Fong said in a statement.

Each year, the state treasurer names firms to underwriting, bond counsel and financial advisory pools. Those firms handle state and authority bond deals. Only firms in the pools are eligible to compete for the business.
The Small Business Enterprise Program is designed to increase the number of smaller firms represented in the state bond pools, where they can compete for the deals.

To qualify for the program, a firm must be based in California and must be independently owned and operated. A firm's most recent three-year average of total gross revenues must be below $5 million per year, Fong said.
Fong said the program would give smaller firms the opportunity to compete, adding "that's critical when you are up against larger firms."
Firms must apply by May 14 to participate in the program.
